Hi Anna — great to chat earlier. Quick recap + next steps from our call with your security and procurement teams:

- Thanks for walking us through AcmeCorp's data residency and compliance checklist.
- Action items we agreed: share our current subprocessor inventory, SOC 2 evidence, and a short data flow summary for your review.
- You asked for cloud provider regions, which subprocessors handle logging/monitoring, and whether we support customer-managed KMS.

Attached: Redwood_Subprocessors_20260630.xlsx and Redwood_Security_FAQ.pdf — the top sheet lists primary cloud providers and common third parties (Datadog, S3, GCS, Cloudflare, Snowflake where applicable).

Quick answers to unblock you while we prepare a slightly more detailed data flow diagram:
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains a current SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period 2025); happy to share the report under an NDA if preferred — link below.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support data processing agreements and can provide HIPAA addendum language for covered deployments.
- Subprocessors: primary compute/storage in GCP (us-west1) and AWS (us-east-1) for certain customers; monitoring and logging typically go to Datadog and S3/GCS buckets.
- Customer-managed keys: available for Dedicated and Private deployments; we support KMS integrations (GCP KMS, AWS KMS, and external HSM via Bring-Your-Own-Key options).

Next steps:
1) I will circulate an updated subprocessor spreadsheet with region annotations and whether subprocessors process PII.
2) Aditya will draft recommended answers for your questionnaire and confirm any documentation links we should send.
3) Please send your vendor security questionnaire (spreadsheet or Doc) and procurement contact if we should loop them in.

Thanks — I'll follow up later today with the updated subprocessor file.

Marissa / Dev — drafting suggested responses for Anna's questions below. Please review/edit before I send to Acme.

1) Regions: primary production footprints are GCP (us-west1, europe-west1) and AWS (us-east-1) for backup/edge in some accounts. EU residency: we can provision eu-only Dedicated or Private deployments; indicate that for EU-bound data we can restrict to europe-west1 and avoid cross-region backup by request.

2) Logs: application logs sent to Datadog are filtered by default. PII is redacted in structured logs; request/response payloads that may contain PII are not sent to Datadog. We retain logs according to customer-configurable retention; default 30 days for metrics/traces, 90 days for error logs; can extend on request. 

3) Payload storage: Redwood stores request/response payloads in encrypted object storage only when caching is enabled (prefix/KV cache). For Hosted customers, ephemeral caches are enabled by default and retention is short (configurable). For Dedicated/Private we follow customer policy.

4) SOC 2: we have a SOC 2 Type II report for 2025. We generally share under NDA; we can provide a secure Drive link to Acme's security team.

Recommended attachments to send: updated subprocessor sheet (add regions + PII processing column), short data flow paragraph, link to SOC 2 under NDA.

I'll prepare a one-page data flow blurb and update the spreadsheet.

— Aditya

Hi Anna — thanks for the list. Per Aditya's notes, please find attached an updated subprocessor inventory and short answers to your questions below. I highlighted the rows that process PII.

Attachments: Redwood_Subprocessors_20260708_updated.xlsx (xlsx)

Short answers (summary):
- Cloud regions: GCP (us-west1, europe-west1) are our primary production regions. We can restrict a customer's deployment to europe-west1 for EU residency requirements (Dedicated/Private recommended).
- Logging/Monitoring: Datadog collects metrics and traces; application logs sent to Datadog are filtered by default. Request/response payloads that may contain PII are NOT sent to Datadog or Sentry. Error logs that include snippets are redacted on ingestion and stored encrypted in S3/GCS.
- Payload storage & retention: By default, Hosted deployments use short-lived KV/prefix caching for performance; retention defaults are 7 days for request cache and configurable per-customer. We can disable caching or configure retention per contract.
- SOC 2: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report (2025). Sharing: we can provide a secure read-only Drive link under an NDA. If Acme would like the report shared directly with Procurement, let me know and I can request an NDA / provide the link.
- Customer-managed KMS: Supported for Dedicated/Private; integration with GCP KMS or AWS KMS or external HSMs is available.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether Procurement would like the SOC 2 under NDA or a copy sent directly.
2) If you share an editable copy of the vendor questionnaire, we will populate the security/infra tabs and return.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute follow-up with Aditya if your security team wants to dive deeper.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
